source_title: Interview with RaBitQ Authors: The TurboQuant Dispute and Why the Storage Selloff Was a False Alarm

source_title: Zilliz Cloud On-Demand Compute: Pay Only for What You Use

source_title: milvus: RBAC grantee-id uses truncated MD5 (64-bit), enabling privilege-binding collisions and cross-role privilege forgery
claim_summary: CVE-2026-10814 (low; CVSS 3.1 4.5): Milvus up to 2.6.13 derived RBAC grantee IDs from a truncated 64-bit MD5, enabling privilege-binding collisions; fixed by commit 3d932f1 (2026-06-02)
limitation: Local attack, high complexity per advisory; CNA is VulDB, GitHub-reviewed; advisory says the exploit was disclosed publicly; no exploitation-in-the-wild data; fixed release version not named in the advisory; NVD API returned HTTP 429 (not used)

source_title: Introducing Loon: A New Storage Engine for Vector Data That Never Stops Changing
claim_summary: Introduces Loon, a manifest-based (Avro-encoded manifest) columnar storage engine on object storage for Milvus 3.0 and Vector Lakebase, defaulting to the open Vortex format; Milvus 3.0 blog later reports internal per-point-read I/O falling from ~9.4 MB (Parquet) to 0.07 MB (Vortex+Loon), 'roughly 135 times less'
availability: ships in Milvus 3.0 (beta May 9, GA Jul 29)
limitation: Internal benchmark only (3M rows, 128-dim, 256 readers per vendor); re-announced by press release 2026-06-29 (same event); Hacker News submission 2026-06-05 had 3 points and 0 comments

source_title: Import bypasses collection-level RBAC and reads Milvus internal storage
claim_summary: Medium (CVSS 3.1 6.5; CWE-22, CWE-863): a user holding Import on one collection could point files[].paths at other collections' internal binlogs and read them; backup/l0_import now need a new cluster-level ImportBinlog privilege; fixed in 2.6.25 and 3.0.3

source_title: Jev's Cheap Decisions Make Semantic Caching Worth Another Try
